candidates.exact_span: effluent limitations for total suspended solids (TSS) at monthly average of 20 mg/l and daily maximum of 30 mg/l. Therefore, based on these similar permitted facilities, using BPJ, effluent limitations for TSS are established in the draft permit identical to the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes enforceable numeric TSS concentration limits (monthly average and daily maximum) and the BPJ basis for their applicability; a different reading of whether these limits are operative, final, or tied to the previous permit could change which limits are compared against reported TSS measurements and whether exceedances are evaluated.

candidates.exact_span: Loading limits are not established since the discharge is not a continuous one and is discharged from a holding lagoon on an as needed basis. This is identical to the previous permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Declares that mass loading limits are not applicable and characterizes discharge as intermittent from a holding lagoon on an as-needed basis; interpreting discharge frequency or continuity differently could change whether loading-based limits apply (A), whether monitoring is required only upon discharge (B), and how missing or no-result periods are classified as no-discharge versus unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: Where these technology-based permit limits do not protect water quality or the designated uses, additional water quality-based effluent limitations and/or conditions are included in the NPDES permits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the trigger for imposing water quality-based effluent limits beyond technology-based controls; whether TBELs are deemed protective affects whether additional numeric WQBELs must be included in the applicable limit set for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: 40 CFR §122.4(d) requires NPDES permits also be protective of a downstream state or tribe’s water quality standards, due to the nature of the discharge being from a water treatment plant, the low (0.177 MGD) volume of discharges, dilution with first the Animas River and then the San Juan River, and distance prior to entering the Navajo Nation, the water quality standards of the Navajo Nation will not be affected
candidates.computation_change_reason: Concludes downstream Navajo Nation water quality standards are not affected based on discharge volume, dilution, and distance; a different interpretation of the dilution analysis or downstream-protection obligation could change whether additional WQBELs or conditions beyond the stated TSS limits are required.

candidates.exact_span: The discharge from the facility may enter Lower Animas Ditch / Hampton Arroyo and/or Williams Arroyo in Water body
candidates.computation_change_reason: Identifies possible receiving waters with uncertainty ('may enter' and multiple arroyos); which water body is the actual discharge point determines which state narrative and numerical water quality standards govern and thus which limits may be derived or required.

candidates.exact_span: General criteria are applicable as specified in 20.6.4.13 NMAC.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies which general New Mexico surface-water criteria apply to the discharge; interpreting the scope or applicability of 20.6.4.13 NMAC general criteria differently could change whether narrative or additional numeric limits supplement the stated TSS effluent limits.
